newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh to set up barge-mounted power plants.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh to set up barge-mounted power plants.

text.p: Power-starved Bangladesh will have three new barge-mounted electricity plants with a total capacity of 300 megawatts (MW) within the next year, Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina told parliament on Tuesday.
"It would be possible to supply 300 MW of electricity in (the) next one year from three barge-mounted plants," she said in reply to a question from opposition legislator Zafrul Islam.
"Each plant will have (the) capacity to generate 100 MW of electricity."
Hasina said her government was also considering a proposal to install a 250-300 MW coal-fired thermal power plant in the next three-and-a-half years to further boost power supply.
Private investors would be allowed to set up a 300-450 MW capacity power station at Meghnaghat near Narayanganj port town, she added.
Energy ministry officials earlier had said the Asian Development Bank and foreign firms would set up the plant in three years with equity participation.

Plans were also underway to install a 100 MW power station at Baghabari in the northern district of Sirajganj, a 300 MW plant at Garipur near Narayanganj and a 200 MW plant in the southern district of Khulna.
Officials said the current power shortfall was up to 350 MW during peak hours, which they blamed largely on the closure of two 270 MW capacity power plants.
They said peak demand for power would rise from the present 2,200 MW to 3,150 MW by the year 2000 and 4,600 MW by 2005.
